title: Severe Weather and Cyclone/Storm Hazard Assessment
source: India National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) & FEMA Severe Weather Safety
summary: Observation guidelines for storm damage, high wind impacts, and fallen trees.
content: Severe cyclonic or convective weather produces multi-dimensional hazards including wind-borne debris, uprooted trees, and sheared utility infrastructure. Critical observational reporting elements include: 1. Roadway passability for emergency response apparatus (ambulances/fire engines). 2. Tangled power cables or transformers sparking on wet pavement. 3. Roof damage, displaced tin sheets, or shattered glass storefronts. 4. Presence of sheltered individuals in non-reinforced structures. Maintain extreme caution around downed power lines (assume all lines are energized).
key_points: Assume all downed cables and metal fences are actively energized
Report flying debris hazards and roof integrity loss
Maintain sheltered perimeter during active severe squalls
